newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: STATE'S STAKE IN BALTIC SHIPYARD TO BE SOLD.
newsitem.headline: STATE'S STAKE IN BALTIC SHIPYARD TO BE SOLD.

text.p: Lithuania's privatisation commission said on Wednesday that it has decided to sell the state's stake in the Baltic Shipyard on the country's stock exchange in June.

"The privatisation of the portfolio of state-run shares in the shipyard will be sold by auction on the Vilnius stock exchange in the period between June 7 and August 7," Vytis Atkochiunas, the director of the privatisation agency, told Reuters.
The state currently has a 32.5 percent stake in the company.
"The portfolio will include 1,125,719 shares with face a value of 10 litas and the initial price for the share portfolio in the auction will be 11.26 million litas," Atkochiunas added.
Denmark's Odensse company acquired 43.6 percent of the company's shares in a block trade on the Vilnius bourse in April.
The company's shareholders' meeting decided to double the share capital to 69.18 million litas and have registered the new share issue with the country's securities commission.
The term when the current shareholders have the priority right to acquire a propotional stake in the new issue expires on June 15, Atkochiunas said.
He also said that the transport ministry has not made a final decision on whether to buy into the new issue.
The Baltic Shipyard is an A group company on the Vilnius bourse.
